tool.name: faToTwoBit

param.name: no_mask
param.label: Ignore soft-masking
param.help: Store all bases as upper case. By default, lower-case (soft-masked) bases stay lower case.

tool.help:
**What it does**
faToTwoBit converts a FASTA file to the [2bit format](https://genome.ucsc.edu/FAQ/FAQformat.html#format7). A 2bit file stores each base in two bits. It also records runs of N and soft-masked (lower-case) regions. Genome browsers can read any region of a 2bit file without reading the whole file. An assembly hub needs a 2bit file for each genome (the `twoBitPath` setting in `genomes.txt`).
-----
**Input**
A nucleotide FASTA file, plain or gzip-compressed. Sequence names must be unique.
**Output**
A 2bit file.
**Options**
- **Ignore soft-masking** (`-noMask`): store all bases as upper case.
A standard 2bit file cannot be larger than 4 GB. The tool uses the 64-bit 2bit format (`-long`) when the input is larger than 4 GB, or larger than 1 GB if it is gzip-compressed. Some older programs cannot read the 64-bit format.
-----
**More information**
- [faToTwoBit source code](https://github.com/ucscGenomeBrowser/kent/tree/master/src/utils/faToTwoBit) - [Assembly hub guide](https://genome.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/help/hubQuickStartAssembly.html)
